learning_outcomes.text: Apply the basic laws of physics and thermodynamics for the analysis of energy conversion machines and systems.
Gain insight into the operation, application possibilities, and efficiencies of piston and turbomachines and thermodynamic cycles.
Become acquainted with the designs of machines and systems in these domains.
Process and apply the theory further during exercise sessions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and basic equations: integral equations for continuity, momentum, angular momentum, 1st and 2nd law of thermodynamics.
Flows through pipes: nozzles and diffusers, Fanno and Rayleigh transformations and normal shock waves
Basic principles of compression and expansion machines: polytropic law and multi-stage compression
Volumetric machines: piston pumps and other volumetric pumps, maximum suction head, piston compressors and other volumetric compressors
Turbomachines: centrifugal and axial pumps, fans and compressors, scaling laws, hydraulic turbines, steam turbines, gas turbines: applications and operational problems
Power generation: Rankine, Brayton, process improvement by application of regeneration, reheating, combined processes (CCGT, CHP), internal combustion engines
Refrigeration machines: compression refrigeration machine and inverse Brayton cycle
System characteristics and scaling laws of pumps (Practicum)
Operation of CHP, energy balance of combustion (Practicum)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

assessment_rules: The exam tests both theoretical aspects and the ability to apply the learned material. The exam consists of open and closed questions. Students are allowed to use a formula sheet and a calculator.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
